Why does the Report editor no longer update the rendered report live?

Long image

A

Answer

Since #82 (2026-08-31), the inline Report editor writes into a nested Formik inside ReportSectionEntityInstance, while the rendered sections read the report Formik. The display only catches up after a save.

  1. #82 added the nested Formik to show virtual attributes without writing them into the Report form, not for performance.1
  2. The Report entity has no virtual attributes, so for the Report editor the nested Formik only isolates the edits.2
  3. That isolation also confines each keystroke to one editor. Removing it everywhere brings the June per-keystroke cost back to every instance page.3
  4. A bypass scoped to the Report editor, plus narrower typecheck dependencies, restores live feedback with the smallest blast radius.

Applies tomiroir-standalone-app at 958657e97 compared with 11d616014 (June sandbox)found by code reading and git historynot reproduced in a running appno timings measured

1

Which Formik does the Report editor write to?

Diagram structure
  • Author author
  • Local cache cache
  • RootComponent root
  • ReportDisplay display
  • ReportViewWithEditor rvwe
  • Report Formik reportFormik
  • Rendered sections sections
  • InlineReportEditor inline
  • Nested Formik nested
  • Report editor fields fields
  • cache → root · model
  • root → display · Report
  • display → rvwe · reportDefinition
  • rvwe → reportFormik · initialValues
  • reportFormik → sections · values[reportName]
  • reportFormik → inline · the Report
  • inline → nested · seeds once
  • author → fields · types
  • fields → nested · every keystroke
  • nested → cache · save only
  1. ReportViewWithEditor ↗

    Puts the displayed Report into the Report Formik under its name.

  2. Rendered sections ↗

    Read the section tree from that key on every render.

  3. InlineReportEditor ↗

    Passes the same key to ReportSectionEntityInstance as the instance to edit.

  4. Nested Formik ↗

    Copies the Report once; with no virtual attributes the copy is identical.

  5. Report editor fields ↗

    Write every keystroke into the copy, which the sections never read.

The June design had one Formik per report page, and every editor in a section consumed it.4 The multistep branch still works that way; every other Report takes the nested branch.2

What happens between a keystroke and the display?

Diagram structure

  • Report Formik reportFormik
  • Rendered sections sections
  • author → fields · types a section label
  • fields → reportFormik · setFieldValue(reportName)

  • reportFormik → fields · re-render and typecheck

Diagram structure
  • Author author
  • Report editor fields fields
  • Nested Formik nested
  • Local cache cache
  • Report Formik reportFormik
  • Rendered sections sections
  • author → fields · types a section label
  • fields → nested · setFieldValue(reportName)
  • nested → fields · re-render and typecheck
  • author → fields · clicks save
  • nested → cache · updateInstance via Report submit
  • cache → reportFormik · new Report, reinitialise
  • reportFormik → sections · re-render with the edit
  • reportFormik → nested · new instance, reinitialise

The save goes through submitNestedFormValues, which strips virtual attributes and calls the Report form's submit.6 The local cache applies the update at once, so the display changes after the save, before any store commit.7

Issue #274 named the isolation ("Edits do not land in the parent Report Formik") but kept it for other Reports.8 #330 listed "no nested Formik for this branch" as an alternative and chose to reroute the submit.9 Neither looked at the Report editor's live display.

4

Why do multistep Reports skip the nested Formik?

They skip it for a functional reason: the wizard must read instance edits before any save, just as the rendered sections must read Report edits.

  1. Step bag keys

    The host keeps one key per object-instance section, its section path joined with _.

  2. Report Formik

    The host copies those keys out of the report Formik on every change and every render.

  3. Next and Finish

    Next feeds the bag to the next step's query; Finish passes it to the composite action.

  4. Nested Formik

    Edits kept in a nested copy would never reach the bag, so Finish would save the seeded value.

The host reads the bag key from the section path10 and fills the bag from the report Formik.11 Finish then runs the action with that bag.12 Decision D5 limits the bag to input values and instance values.13 Slice 4 chose "one write path": the instance editor writes the report Formik directly.14

What the bypass does not cover

The check reads the type of the Report that contains the section. For the inline Report editor that is reportReportDetails, so the editor always takes the nested branch, even on a multistep Report. Keeping the nested Formik elsewhere was a scope choice ("so we do not change current instance pages"), not a technical need.8

  • multistep.274.phase0.unit.test.ts checks by regex that <Formik … onSubmit={submitNestedFormValues} exists.

  • The report.bookDetails MiroirTest saves an edited title and refuses an invalid one.
  • No test checks that a Report edit shows in the rendered sections before save.
6

Why not simply revert #82's Formik?

In a shared Formik, every section re-renders on each keystroke, and every TypedValueObjectEditor re-runs mlsTypeCheck, because its memo depends on the whole formik.values.3 With the editor open, that includes a full typecheck of the Report value. Nobody has measured this cost, in June or now.

OptionLive Report editorLive Query test runTyping cost on instance pagesBlast radius
A. Remove the nested FormikRestoredYesYesHigherJune cost on every pageWidest; breaks 2 tests; virtual attributes need a new display path
B1. Bypass for the Report editor onlyRestoredYesNoSameUnchangedSmallest; like the multistep bypass
B2. Nest only when virtual attributes are overlaidRestoredYesYesHigherJune cost for all entities but BookMedium
C. Keep nesting, mirror into the Report FormikYesYesBoth Formiks re-renderRiskyTwo sources of truth; reinitialise ping-pong
D. Drop formik.values from the typecheck memon/an/aLowerOne typecheck per keystroke instead of one per editorLow; the typecheck reads only its own value

Recommended: B1 with D, then decide whether the Query page needs B2.

7

What was never live, even in June?

  • Query edits: the report query is built from props.reportDefinition, so extractor changes need a save.16
  • Markdown content: the section copies its content into local state at mount.
  • Code-editor fields: their text stays local until it parses as JSON.
  • Unsaved edits: any deep change of report data reinitialises the Report Formik and drops them.
8

Which component does what?

ReportViewWithEditor (RVWE)
Builds the report query and creates the report Formik
ReportSectionViewWithEditor (RSVWE)
Renders one section from the report Formik; recurses into grids, lists and accordions
ReportSectionEntityInstance (RSEI)
Shows one entity instance; mounts the nested Formik since #82
TypedValueObjectEditor (TVOE)
Schema-driven editor of the nearest Formik; runs mlsTypeCheck and owns the save button
InlineReportEditor
Report editor shown above the sections when edit mode is on
Report Formik
One form state per report page: section data, query results, and the Report under its name
Nested Formik
One-key copy of an instance, used for every Report except multistep ones
Step bag
What a multistep user entered; Next and Finish pass it to queries and actions
Save
updateInstance applied to the local cache at once
Commit
Persists the open transaction to the store
